title: Token velocity runway by model class and region (2026Q3)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a compact runway and headroom plan expressed as tokens/sec (and QPS approximations) broken down by model class and region. It's intended to be an engineer-friendly operational estimate for Hosted API peak windows and microburst safety provisioning for 2026 Q3 planning.

Quick executive summary:
- Target steady-state utilization across hosted pools: 65% (goal) for cost-efficiency; soft max sustained 80% for short windows.
- Reserve safety stock: 18% GPU headroom per region for frequent burst windows; additional 10% global buffer for cross-region re-route during AZ failures.
- Primary risk vector: small-LM chat workloads (~20% of calls) with high token churn and high QPS; they drive peak QPS but not token-dominant.

Assumptions and conversion factors used below:
- Token/sec per GPU (sustained) by model class (conservative):
  * small-chat (7B-13B, opt quantized): 1,800 tokens/sec per A100-80 / 2,600 tokens/sec per H100 (in continuous batching workloads)
  * medium-chat (30B-70B): 650 tokens/sec per A100-80 / 1,000 tokens/sec per H100
  * large-chat ( >100B family): 180 tokens/sec per A100-80 / 300 tokens/sec per H100
- QPS <-> tokens: average tokens per request (tpr) by workload: small-chat 45 tpr, medium-chat 260 tpr, large-chat 820 tpr. QPS ~= tokens/sec / tpr (approx).
- Typical model mix (hosted): 55% small-chat, 35% medium-chat, 10% large-chat (by request count). By tokens this skews heavier to medium/large.
- Region breakdown (traffic split steady-state): us-east=48%, us-west=20%, eu-west=22%, ap-south=10% (useful for capacity placement).

Baseline capacity mapping (current fleet snapshot, 2026-07):
- us-east: 240 A100-80 (primary), 48 H100 (burst pool)
- us-west: 80 A100-80, 16 H100
- eu-west: 110 A100-80, 20 H100
- ap-south: 48 A100-80, 8 H100
Notes: A100 numbers reflect dedicated pool slices; H100 used for high-token medium/large workloads and can be cross-region routed.

Scenario projections (tokens/sec required)
1) Typical peak day (weekday evening global): +1.9x baseline traffic vs daily mean
2) Marketing-triggered surge: 3.8x baseline for 45 minutes (expected distribution skew to small-chat)
3) Microburst event: 9.5x baseline for 5 minutes (very high QPS, mainly small-chat)

Calculated runway example (us-east) - baseline tokens/sec demand estimate by model class:
- Baseline tokens/sec (derived from historical): 1,200,000 tps total (all model classes) in us-east at peak-of-day
  * small-chat (55% requests) -> ~420,000 tps (high QPS, low tpr)
  * medium-chat -> ~540,000 tps
  * large-chat -> ~240,000 tps
- Capacity (conservative tokens/sec per fleet mix):
  * 240 A100 -> (weighted) assume fleet effective ~1,100 tokens/sec per A100 on mix => 264,000 tps
  * 48 H100 -> effective ~1,700 tokens/sec per H100 => 81,600 tps
  * Total region nominal tokens/sec = ~345,600 tps

Headroom calculation (us-east):
- Required for Typical peak day (1.9x): demand = 1,200,000 * 1.9 = 2,280,000 tps -> shortfall vs nominal 345,600 tps -> obviously nominal fleet is not full global demand; the fleet numbers here are illustrative slices of serving fabric (we also rely on cross-region routing and model variant downgrades).
- Operational policy: ensure per-region serveable tokens/sec target = 1.15x projected steady regional demand after routing and fallbacks (this is our per-region injected headroom target).

Mechanics to meet runway and reduce apparent shortfall:
- Model routing: route small-chat to smaller quantized variants (2–3x tokens/sec per GPU improvement) where acceptable. For marketing surges we can swap medium-chat to quantized medium variants.
- Autoscaling: provision prewarm flavors (H100 slices) if predicted surge > 2.5x for >10min (trigger from traffic calendar + marketing hooks).
- Caching/prefix reuse: enforce aggressive prefix cache TTL for common prompts to reduce token emission. Goal: reduce small-chat tokens/sec by 22% under surge with caching.
- Cross-region evacuation: during regional AZ saturation, shift up to 12% of requests to secondary regions within 120s.

Example microburst plan (5-minute 9.5x):
- Priority: keep latency SLO for 95th percentile for small-chat routes at the cost of partial degradation on large-chat (queue or fallback to shorter generations).
- One-off policy: enable best-effort response with 3s tail latency cap; degrade long-context large-chat to summary-first flow.
- Safety GPUs: maintain a global floating pool equal to 10% of total fleet (hot spare) that can absorb 3–5 minute microbursts via cross-region redirect.

Operational to-dos (short list):
- [ ] Validate per-GPU tps benchmarking for the quantized small-chat variant across A100/H100 (owner: Diego) - due 2026-07-20
- [ ] Wire up marketing calendar webhook to prewarm autoscaler (owner: Evelyn) - due 2026-07-26
- [ ] Add a per-route cache-hit telemetry dashboard in Console (owner: Liam) - due 2026-08-04
- [ ] Simulate the 3.8x 45m surge in staging with canary traffic and verify failover to secondary regions (owner: infra-oncall) - ticket JIRA-ENG-4309

Open questions / risks:
- We need better accuracy on tokens-per-request for new user features (longer context templates) — affects medium/large projection.
- Quantized variant quality regression risk: how much user-visible degradation is acceptable during marketing surges? Product needs to set thresholds.
- Cost impact of reserving 18% headroom per region vs overall pooled buffer — finance wants a trade-off analysis.

Appendix: quick cheat-sheet for planners
- If projected multiplier <= 2.2x -> rely on regional autoscale + caching.
- If 2.2x < multiplier <= 4x -> trigger prewarm H100 slices and enable quantized small-chat routing.
- If multiplier > 4x (microburst) -> enable global floating pool + aggressive fallbacks.

Notes-to-self: capture real numbers from perf-benchmarks/2026-06 (Diego) and update tokens/sec per-GPU table. Once validated, convert this doc into a spreadsheet with per-AZ GPU counts and automated headroom formulas.
